answer: A graph-anomaly detector can wall off a garden of agent accounts by scoring each new node on its neighborhood's label-homogeneity and timing coherence against the verified core. It flags clusters whose cedar of trust links to already-flagged accounts exceeds a calibrated cut, forcing attackers to buy and age many unrelated edges, which raises cost sharply. This fable of cheap sybils breaks when adversaries genuinely mix with honest hubs, so the mechanism bounds rather than eliminates infiltration.
